summary:
A twin-gabled half-timbered burgage warehouse runs right through the block. It is dark oak frame with white calcite daub under two steep slate gables, and both street faces are the same: hoist beams and stacked loading doors in each gable, and two jettied storeys over a ground floor of open shop counters. The six wood merchants are meshed back to back, three per street, each dressed in its own wood, with a stair lobby at the west end and a cart passage through the block at the east end. Twin-gabled half-timbered Hanseatic Speicher running street to street: back-to-back rows of three wood merchants each (oak, spruce, birch north; jungle, acacia, dark oak south) under two jettied storeys of dark-oak frame and calcite, slate gables with hoist beams.
West stair lobby and counting room, east cart passage, keepers' gallery over the meshed pockets.
Five neutral roles (frame, infill, trim, base, roof) for reskinning; shop woods stay with the decorator.

Shell and floors: Shell and floors built in parts/shell.mjs and make.sh gives a whole build.nbt: paved streets and alleys, calcite and frame end-bay walls with plinth, cart arches, passage ceiling, floor slabs y12 and y18, gallery partitions z14 and z23, hatches with ladders, stairs 1 and 2. make.sh showed no REFUSED or off-palette lines. The Lobby, Stair hall and Counting room walk as ok; the last full walk output I read was cut off after Pocket A1, so I haven't confirmed the rest. I didn't render the tiles.
polish: I did not render the tiles, so I haven't looked at how the part reads.
The last mcd walk output I read stopped at Pocket A1. The remaining rooms (pockets, cart passage, stores, gallery, loft) are unconfirmed.

I did not re-run mcd walk or the other checks after the final change. I did not confirm the six ladders at y11 are now supported. That change was six dark_oak_planks cells at (11,11,15), (19,11,15), (27,11,15) and (15,11,22), (23,11,22), (31,11,22).
The first check showed 1848 floating blocks in the roof. The Timber frame part is still a stub, so no upper walls exist yet.
Doorways at x3..4 and x20..21 (y13..15) are cut in both gallery partitions. This is my addition, so stair 1 and stair 2 connect.
The west bay is one open hall with no partitions: the lobby, stair hall and counting room boxes meet with no wall between them.
Windows at x3 and x7 (y6..8) and the door and transom cells (x5..6, y5..7) in the west-bay street walls are left as air for the fittings part.
Room floors (lobby polished_andesite, plank floors) are not laid; the podium cobblestone is still the floor. The room designers need to replace it.

make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; the Timber frame line shows 1726 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. Front render reads as Tudor half-timber with two gables and jetties.

Gable loading doors at y25..27 on x11..12 and x30..31 (P5) collide with the gable king posts that gableFrame builds there; the doors will be refused unless the king posts move or the doors are dropped.
Loft and first-floor loading doors (P5): the frame leaves x11..12 and x30..31 open at the door bays and adds lintels at y16 and y22; the doors' transoms (y15, y21) and the leaves are P5's.
Side windows (x2 and x40) are left as air at z 7, 19, 31 for P5 to glaze, not placed here; plan's z 9, 21, 29 are posts, so the deviation is noted in plan.md.
The loft and first-floor timber store items in elements.md stay unticked until P5 adds their windows and loading doors.

Walkability and the stair hall/loft interior were not checked by me; mcd check reported no floating or unsupported blocks from the frame. The 24 orphan smooth_stone_slab blocks in the check output come from another part (counters), not the frame.

Side windows are at z 11, 19, 27 rather than the plan's z 9, 21, 29 (those are frame post lines). Noted in plan.md Notes.
Lanterns at (11,25,1), (30,25,1), (11,25,36), (30,25,36) report as floating and unsupported in mcd check, because the hoist chains they hang from are P2's hoistBeam, which is still a stub here.

summary: inspection: Lumber Hall, between-parts pass: make.sh passes and build.nbt is whole. Fixed the pavement (56 dark cells to 0, four lamp posts added), and the off-palette counter block (smooth_stone_slab to polished_andesite_slab via sockets.json fitout). Not fixed: six keeper pockets (A1-A3, B1-B3) still read "no way in", because the walker treats the open hatch trapdoors as solid, so the verdict is a toolkit gap rather than a build fault.
polish: Six pocket rooms still UNREACHABLE in mcd walk (A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3; walk ok:false). Cause: the keeper hatches (11,12,16) (19,12,16) (27,12,16) (15,12,21) (23,12,21) (31,12,21) are open dark_oak_trapdoor blocks, and rooms.mjs PASS has no trapdoor entry, so the walker treats them as solid. Proof: clearing those six cells in a copy (/tmp, build untouched) made all six pockets 6/6 reached and walk ok:true. The game passes open trapdoors, so I believe the pockets are reachable in play, but I could not run the game to confirm. I did not change the plan's trapdoor hatches to holes, and did not edit the shared toolkit. Decision needed: (a) teach rooms.mjs and room-check.mjs that an open trapdoor is passable, or (b) make the six hatch cells plain holes. The sockets check's 12 'keeper can't reach' warnings have the same root cause.

Version mismatch: the file's DataVersion is 4189 (1.21.4), where the chain block id is 'chain'. The palette and the hoist/lantern chains (room-1, room-3, room-8, room-12, frame hoistBeam via IRON_CHAIN) use 'iron_chain', which mcd info flags as unknown. Palette rules say keep iron_chain, so this needs a project decision (pin the target version to 26.x, or change the palette). Not changed.
mcd check reports 22 orphans, all designed shop counters (polished_andesite_slab, double, at y5 in front of each payment hopper). They are supported and not floating, so I left them.
